rows.text: The rear lamp shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the rear lamp shall be clearly legible.
All markings on the rear lamp shall be indelible.
With regard to the size of the approval marking on the rear lamp, the value for "a" shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking of the rear lamp shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking of the rear lamp shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number of the approval marking of the rear lamp shall be placed close to the approval mark.

The approval marking of the rear lamp shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.

If the rear lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the approval marking shall include, as an additional symbol, a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
If the rear lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the arrow on the rear position lamp shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.

If the rear lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, in the case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, the arrow on the reversing lamp shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The rear lamp shall bear the approval marking.
The rear lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Except where the rear lamp has non-replaceable light sources, the rear lamp shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Except where the rear lamp has non-replaceable light sources, if the rear lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), the rear lamp shall also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
The approval marking shall consist of:.
In the case of lamps with an electronic light source control gear, the rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In the case of lamps with a variable luminous intensity control, the rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In the case of lamps with a secondary operating mode, the rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In the case of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, the rear lamp shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the specific identification code shall comprise the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1.
In case several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the approval mark on the module and the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used shall be from the same applicant, although the marks do not have to be the same.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the rear lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the rear lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the rear lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number.
An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the rear lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the rear lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
In any case, the approval marking shall be visible when the rear lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.

In any case, the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the rear lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of the rear lamp is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on the detachable lens.
If the outer lens of the rear lamp is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the rear lamp.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps bear a single approval mark, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
The rear lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The rear lamp shall meet the requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval.

The rear lamp shall meet the requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The rear lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured.

The rear lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, it retains the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, the rear position lamp and stop lamp functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source), or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, a note shall be made within the communication document, in either case.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, the light intensity of the rear lamp shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and, when all light sources are illuminated, the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or, alternatively, provision (b) shall apply.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, where provision (a) is not applied, a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced.

Where a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure is produced, a note in the communication form shall state that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

The rear lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).

In case a light source category or categories or type(s) is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, the applicant for type approval of the rear lamp shall declare that the lamp is only intended for installation on those vehicles.

In case a light source category or categories or type(s) is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, the declaration shall be noted in the communication form.
In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the design of the rear lamp shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light source(s) holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, and the holder data sheet relevant to the category of light source(s) prescribed applies.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s), where a category of LED substitute light source(s) is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to the category of LED substitute light source(s) shall apply.
The rear lamp shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances, which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
In the case of replaceable UN approved light sources, all measurements of the rear lamp shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.
In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements of the rear lamp shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

In case of a lamp (function) using light sources which are subject to more than one of the conditions prescribed in paragraph 4.8., the photometric measurements of the rear lamp shall be made separately, in accordance with each applicable condition(s) set forth in paragraph 4.8.

In case of a lamp (function) using light sources which are subject to more than one of the conditions prescribed in paragraph 4.8., all separate measurement results of the rear lamp shall be added together.
If not otherwise specified, the intensities of the rear lamp shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the rear lamp shall be operated as specified by the applicant.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear lamp shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear lamp shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear lamp shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5., by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, as an alternative, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear lamp shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear lamp shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for the rear lamp.

If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously at the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.

If one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated lamps contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp, the values to be considered for the rear lamp shall be those obtained with all sources in operation.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities of the rear lamp shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear lamp shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3.
To check the colorimetric characteristics of the rear lamp, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed for the rear lamp.

For a rear lamp equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics of the rear lamp shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.

The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the rear position lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 4, except that a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The rear position lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 4.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the stop lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 7.
The stop lamp shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 7.
The stop lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.

The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the reversing lamp shall meet the requirements in Table 10, except that where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices, the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards where a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, this condition shall be clearly explained in the application for approval and relating documents (see paragraph 3.1.).

Where the type approval is granted applying the condition of verification only up to an angle of 30° inwards, a statement in paragraph 9.1.3. of the communication form (see Annex 1) shall inform that the reversing lamp shall only be installed in a pair.
The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.

If not otherwise specified, the values shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV, which give the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required for the various directions of measurement, shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

If not otherwise specified, where the rear position lamp is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

If not otherwise specified, where the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

If not otherwise specified, within the field of light distribution schematically shown as a grid, the light intensity in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value being shown on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction as a percentage.

If not otherwise specified, in the case of the reversing lamp, if visual examination of the lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, a check shall be made to ensure that no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement is below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.
The reversing lamp shall emit light with the minimum intensities given in figure A3-V for the various directions of measurement.
For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities of the lamp measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, the reversing lamp luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only, for all other lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of the lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, a tolerance of ±3° being allowed.

In the case of all signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, a tolerance of ±3° being allowed.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, in the case where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this requirement not being valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
The illuminating lamps described in paragraphs 2.5.1., 2.5.2. and 2.5.10. shall be so installed that correct adjustment of their orientation can easily be carried out.
In the absence of specific instructions lamps constituting a pair shall:.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except that this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the rear lamp shall satisfy the above requirements so far as is possible.

Where lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, shall be fulfilled.
When all other functions with which the lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF, the photometric and colorimetric requirements of the lamp shall be fulfilled.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.
The maximum height above the ground of the lamp shall be measured from the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
The minimum height above the ground of the lamp shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of the lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Where the photometric characteristics of the lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, which is permitted, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

Where the photometric characteristics of the lamp vary as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, which is permitted, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

Where the photometric characteristics of the lamp vary when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, which is permitted, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by the rear lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

To verify paragraphs 5.10.1. and 5.10.2., for the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

To verify paragraphs 5.10.1. and 5.10.2., for the visibility of white light towards the rear of a vehicle, with the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, when verifying paragraphs 5.10.1. and 5.10.2., the requirement above shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp.
The reversing lamp shall emit white light.
The stop lamp shall emit red light.
The rear position lamp shall emit red light.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
Any lamp may be installed on movable components only if the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.

The rear position lamp and the rear retro-reflector may be installed on movable components only if, at all fixed positions of the movable components, the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.

Where the functions referred to in paragraph 5.18. are obtained by an interdependent lamp system and the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s), the requirements of paragraph 5.18.1. shall be satisfied, except that additional lamps for the above functions may be switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position.

Where the complete interdependent lamp system is mounted on the moving component(s) and additional lamps are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, the additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

Where the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, with the exception of direction indicator lamps, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during the device approval procedure shall meet all the position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).

Where the interdependent lamp system is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, the inwards geometric visibility requirement(s) is(are) deemed to be satisfied if the interdependent lamp(s) still conform(s) to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamp and the rear retro-reflector shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use".

If the requirement that the apparent surface not be hidden more than 50 per cent is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the above indicated lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

As an alternative, if the requirement that the apparent surface not be hidden more than 50 per cent is not practicable, a remark in the communication form (item 10.1. of Annex 1) shall inform other Administrations that more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components.

As an alternative, if the requirement that the apparent surface not be hidden more than 50 per cent is not practicable, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road.

The rear lamp approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance.

The rear lamp approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.
The vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement of the light source of the rear lamp.

Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is provided, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is provided, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.

During replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the rear lamp which, according to its type approval documentation, has been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, in all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the rear lamp shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent.
The provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. and 5.27.2. shall not apply to a rear lamp which includes an electronic light source control gear.
The provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. and 5.27.2. shall not apply to a rear lamp which includes a variable intensity control being part of the device.
The provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. and 5.27.2. shall not apply to a rear lamp which includes only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the rear lamp observed from infinity, except that no account is taken of obstacles if they were already presented when the lamp was type-approved.
If measurements are taken closer to the rear lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the rear lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5º (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5º below the horizontal.

When installed on a vehicle, all lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of this Regulation.

When installed on a vehicle which is approved according to this Regulation and approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128, the lamps shall be fitted with light sources approved according to these light source categories only, except that this requirement does not concern light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except for when they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.
The reversing lamp shall be present on motor vehicles and on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4.
One reversing lamp shall be installed on motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm.
The reversing lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.

The reversing lamp shall be at the rear of the vehicle, except that, if installed, the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. may be fitted on the side of the vehicle, provided that the requirements of paragraphs 6.4.5.2. and 6.4.6.2. below are fulfilled.
For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, the geometric visibility, defined by angles α and β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards.
For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, if there is only one device, the geometric visibility angle β, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be 45° to right and to left.
For reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle, if there are two devices, the geometric visibility angle β, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7., shall be 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
The reversing lamp shall be no special requirement. (in width).

For the two optional reversing lamp devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. if fitted on the side of the vehicle, the geometric visibility shall be considered to be ensured if the reference axis of the respective device is directed outwards with an angle β not exceeding 15° relative to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
If the two optional reversing lamp devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2., are fitted on the side of the vehicle, the provisions of paragraph 6.4.5.2. above shall apply to the reversing lamp.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
If either of the conditions (reverse gear engaged; propulsion system operation possible) is not satisfied, the reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be mandatory on all categories of vehicles.
Stop lamp devices of S3 or S4 category shall be fitted on M1 and N1 categories of vehicles, except for chassis-cabs and those N1 category vehicles with open cargo space.
On all categories of vehicles, two S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be fitted.
On all categories of vehicles, one S3 or S4 category stop lamp device shall be fitted.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For all other categories of vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices, the distance in between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm, except that this distance may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.
For S3 or S4 category stop lamp devices, the centre of reference shall be situated on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle.

Where two stop lamp devices of the S3 or S4 category are installed according to paragraph 6.7.2., the devices shall be positioned as close as possible to the median longitudinal plane, one on each side of this plane.

In the case where one S3 or S4 category stop lamp offset from the median longitudinal plane is permitted according to paragraph 6.7.2., the offset shall not exceed 150 mm from the median longitudinal plane to the centre of reference of the lamp.

The S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground, except that the maximum may be 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed.
If the optional lamps are installed, the optional stop lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

If the optional lamps are installed, the optional stop lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
For S1 or S2 categories devices, the stop lamp shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

For S1 or S2 categories devices, the stop lamp shall have a geometric visibility horizontal angle of 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for the stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
For S3 or S4 categories devices, the stop lamp shall have a geometric visibility horizontal angle of 10° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.

For S1 or S2 categories devices, the stop lamp shall have a geometric visibility vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For S1 or S2 categories devices, the stop lamp shall have a geometric visibility vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
For S3 or S4 categories devices, the stop lamp shall have a geometric visibility vertical angle of 10° above and 5° below the horizontal.
The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
When the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H, all stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously.
Rear position lamp devices of R or R1 or R2 categories shall be mandatory.

The number of rear position lamps shall be two, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

The rear position lamp shall be positioned such that the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane is not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, except that this condition shall not apply to the optional rear lamps.
For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear position lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall have no special requirement.

For all other categories of vehicles, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear position lamps in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm, except that this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

The rear position lamp shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm above the ground, except that the maximum may be 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the symmetry of the lamps.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible.
If the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
The rear position lamp shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

The rear position lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 45° inwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
The rear position lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 80° outwards.

The rear position lamp shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 15° above the horizontal, except that where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

The rear position lamp shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 15° below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where the lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, under the alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, to be considered visible, the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres.
For M1 and N1 category vehicles, under the alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1. above, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
The rear position lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
The rear position lamp shall have a closed-circuit tell-tale.
Except when daytime running lamps are switched ON, the tell-tale of the rear position lamp shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
If required by the component Regulation, the rear position lamp shall have a tell-tale indicating failure.
The rear retro-reflector shall be present on motor vehicles.

The rear retro-reflectors shall be two in number, type-approved according to the requirements concerning Class IA or IB retro-reflectors in the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or in the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4. below) shall not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

The point on the illuminating surface of the rear retro-reflector which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear retro-reflectors in the direction of the reference axes shall have no special requirement.

For all other categories of vehicles, the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces of the rear retro-reflectors in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm, except that this distance may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

The rear retro-reflector shall be not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm above the ground, except that it may be not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), and 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1200 mm respectively.
The rear retro-reflector shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
The rear retro-reflector shall have a horizontal geometric visibility angle of 30° inwards and outwards.
The rear retro-reflector shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 10° above horizontal.

The rear retro-reflector shall have a vertical geometric visibility angle of 10° below horizontal, except that where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The rear retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.

The retro-reflector shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2. or, the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the rear lamp shall be clearly legible.
All markings on the rear lamp shall be indelible.
The approval marking of the rear lamp shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking of the rear lamp shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
Where the approval marking as defined in paragraph 3.3.2. is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown in Figure I.
The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflector shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.4. on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible.
The approval marking shall consist of:.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations and a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier is affixed, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.

The size of the components of a single approval mark on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The retro-reflecting device shall meet the requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval.

Where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible, the retro-reflecting device shall meet the requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the retro-reflecting device is intended to be installed.
The retro-reflective device shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and continues to do so in normal use.
The retro-reflective device shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflective device or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not be rough.
Any protuberances on the outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall not prevent easy cleaning.
When in normal use, there shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector.
In case of retro-reflectors, the combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
In case of retro-reflectors, the colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by means of paint or varnish shall not be permitted.
For the test procedure for night time colours, the specifications shall apply only to white, red or amber retro-reflective devices.

For testing the colour of the retro-reflector, the retro-reflector shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1= β2= 0° or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1. shall be used.

For testing the colour of the retro-reflector, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., the retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., the retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

When tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., the retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
The applicant shall submit ten samples of the retro-reflector for approval, which shall be tested in the chronological order as indicated in paragraph 5.1.7.

After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten retro-reflector samples shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6.

At least one hour after the heat resistance test, the ten retro-reflector samples shall be examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The two retro-reflectors giving the minimum and maximum values shall then be fully tested as shown in paragraph 5.1.4.
These two retro-reflector samples shall be kept by the laboratories for any further checks which may be found necessary.
Four retro-reflector samples out of the remaining eight samples shall be selected at random and divided into two groups of two in each group.
The other eight retro-reflector samples shall be divided into four groups of two.
The two retro-reflector samples of the first group shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6).

If the water penetration test is satisfactory, the two retro-reflector samples of the first group shall then be subjected to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
If necessary, the two retro-reflector samples of the second group shall be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6.
The two retro-reflector samples of the second group shall then be subjected to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The two retro-reflector samples of the third group shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The two retro-reflector samples of the fourth group shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
After undergoing the tests referred to in the paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
After undergoing the tests referred to in the paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4.

After undergoing the tests referred to in the paragraph 5.1.3.1., the verification of the RI of the retro-reflectors shall be performed only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

When applying for approval, the applicant shall specify one or more or a range of axis of reference, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of coefficients of luminous intensity RI of the retro-reflector.

In the case where more than one or a range of different axis of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements of the retro-reflector shall be repeated making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.

For photometric measurements, only the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter for Class IA or IB shall be considered.

For photometric measurements, the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.
The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.
After undergoing the tests referred to in the paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have:.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA and Class IB shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

For Class IA and Class IB retro-reflectors, RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 shall not be permissible within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the following lines: (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).

Where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The testing of the colour of the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

Where the Type Approval Authorities authorize laboratories to omit certain unnecessary tests depending on the nature of the materials of the retro-reflectors and their optical units, the omission shall be mentioned under "Remarks" on the form notifying approval, and the omission shall be applicable only to tests described in Part 3 of Annex 4, in Parts 4, 5 and 6 of Annex 6.
The retro-reflector of Classes IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB shall be tested in the chronological order of tests given in Table 4.
The retro-reflector of Class IVA shall be tested in the chronological order of tests given in Table 5.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', the retro-reflector not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about its axis of reference to the position of minimum RI, which must conform to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.
When the RI is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflector not marked "TOP" shall be placed in the position corresponding to this value of ε.
If the specified values are not attained, the retro-reflector not marked "TOP" may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', the retro-reflector marked "TOP" shall be rotated about its axis ±5°.

With an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', the RI of the retro-reflector marked "TOP" must not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation.

If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements of the retro-reflector for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the retro-reflector of Class IA or IB shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, after the 48-hour period at 65 °C ± 2 °C, the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 ºC.
After the resistance to heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component shall be visible.

The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, or a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.
The immersion test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
After the water immersion test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.

If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, in the case of retro-reflectors, the RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, for retro-reflective devices of the Classes IB and IIIB, the moisture and dust tests shall be applied.
The sample device mounted on a test fixture, with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to a water spray.

If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, during the water spray test these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation.
Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed, or be formable by tapping or tilting the device.
Upon completion of the drain period, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth.
Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

The retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed.

The resistance of the front surface of the retro-reflective device to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

For the resistance to corrosion test, the retro-reflective device, or the rear lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

When a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol is applied to a retro-reflective device, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.

When a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol is applied to a retro-reflective device, after about five minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually.

When a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol is applied to a retro-reflective device, after about five minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

In the test procedure for moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle of type 1, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.

In the test procedure for moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle of type 1, after about 5 minutes, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.

In the test procedure for moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle of type 1, after the surface has been cleaned, the RI shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

In case of an ESA is (part of) a light source, the applicant shall specify the approval number according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128, granted to this ESA, or provide a test report by a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority, stating that this ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
If the representative ESA system(s) fulfil(s) the requirements of paragraph 6. and, if applicable, paragraph 7. of this Regulation, type approval shall be granted.
In case of an ESA is (part of) a light source and if the documentation as specified in paragraph 3.2.10. above is missing, approval of this ESA according to Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.
An approval number shall be assigned to each vehicle or ESA type approved in accordance with Schedule 4 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
An approval mark described in paragraph 5.3. below shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

An international approval mark shall be affixed, in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under this Regulation.
The international approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
A test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied for either:.

The international approval mark on the rear lamp shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1. above.

The rear lamp and its electrical/electronic system(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.
The rear lamp shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions.
The rear lamp shall be tested for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

Before testing, the Technical Service shall prepare a test plan in conjunction with the manufacturer, which contains at least mode of operation, stimulated function(s), monitored function(s), pass/fail criterion(criteria) and intended emissions.

Depending on the intended operating conditions of the propulsion system, the test plan shall define the minimum number of steady state operating conditions of the vehicle, selectable by the driver or by the control system.
The test conditions shall consider multiple propulsion system operating strategies which can be activated permanently by the driver or the vehicle control system.
The test conditions shall be based on documentation provided in Annexes 2A and 2B (e.g. risk analysis).
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband limit for the rear lamp shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband limit for the rear lamp shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the broadband limit for the rear lamp shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m.
On the rear lamp representative of its type, the measured values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the rear lamp representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits for the rear lamp shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limits for the rear lamp shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the limit for the rear lamp in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the rear lamp representative of its type, the measured value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The emission of the rear lamp representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9, with the test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2a.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9, with the test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band given in Table 2b.

The rear lamp representative of its type shall be considered as complying with immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there is no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions".

The immunity of the rear lamp representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 16750-2 for starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.
The starting profile shall be tested on the rear lamp according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1.
The Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 shall be applied to the rear lamp for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

why: variant:does not include an electronic oscillator
rows.text: Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, the rear lamp shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.

why: variant:are not switched, contain no switches
rows.text: Where ESAs are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load, the rear lamp shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7, except that the rear lamp need not be tested for transient conducted emission.
During the radiated broadband emission test, the rear lamp under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.
When the rear lamp is involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the rear lamp shall be in charging mode during the radiated broadband emission test.
During the whole frequency range measurement, the state of charge (SOC) of the traction battery shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of the maximum SOC.
If the test is not performed with a REESS, the rear lamp should be tested at rated current.
If the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 80 per cent of its maximum rated charging/input current value for AC charging.

For DC charging, if the current consumption can be adjusted, the current shall be set to at least 20 per cent of its nominal value or to a minimum of 16 A (if the 20 per cent of its nominal value cannot be achieved in the test facility), unless another value is agreed with the type approval authorities.

For measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS), the limits for radiated broadband emissions of the rear lamp shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.
If peak detectors are used for the radiated broadband emission measurement of the rear lamp, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
During the radiated narrowband emission test, the rear lamp under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

For measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS), the limits for radiated narrowband emissions of the rear lamp shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.

When the rear lamp is in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the rear lamp shall comply with the requirements of the combination of the Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2 and Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4 at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of this Annex being covered.
During the immunity test, the rear lamp under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
Measurements on the rear lamp shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The test signal modulation shall be AM (amplitude modulation), with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The test signal modulation shall be PM2 (pulse modulation type 2), Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.
The test signal modulation shall be PM3 (pulse modulation type 3), Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.
If not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer, the frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.

When tested for immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 shall be applied to the supply lines of the rear lamp as well as to other connections of the rear lamp which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

When tested for immunity against transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, the starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 shall be applied to the supply lines of the rear lamp as well as to other connections of the rear lamp which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except that ESAs exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor) are not subject to the starting profile.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the rear lamp on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 on the supply lines as well as on other connections of the rear lamp which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
